claims: scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:750 — the file grows from 998 to 1,077 lines, crossing the 1,000-line hard cap; docs/pr-checklists/recurring-review-patterns.md:189-194 requires a file pushed past a cap to be split in the same PR

a new sibling module has to be added to `required_runtime_names` in `scripts/agent-autoreview.sh:4319-4325`, otherwise `agent:autoreview` copies the runtime files without it and the import fails there even though local tests pass

docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:399-408 — the closeout step comes after the only projection pair: runs the pair at step 5, posts the request at step 8, and signals all-clear at step 10 with no second pair, contrary to AGENTS.md:90-95 requiring ordered runbooks to match

"Idempotent" overstates what the marker does (.agents/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:310 and .claude mirror, .agents/skills/ship/SKILL.md:214, cloud-watch-loop.md:55, the ADR) — it's a check-then-post: two babysitters can both see `missing` and both post a paid request

Anyone can post the request marker: at `pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-778`, a comment with the mention and marker for the current head counts no matter who wrote it; a spoofed or ignored comment leaves the state stuck at `requested`, so the agent never sends a real request
`classifyCodexReviewSignal` (line 718) has the same gap of accepting a marker comment from any author
A plain `@coderabbitai review` from a human is ignored: the classifier only counts requests carrying the marker (lines 439-441), so it reports `missing` and the agent posts a second paid request
The `gates` block in the JSON example (`pr-ready-state.md:276-298`) lacks `codeRabbitReviewSignal`, so it's now incomplete

`reviewed` needs a PR review whose body has `**Run ID**`; if a clean CodeRabbit follow-up run only edits the walkthrough comment, heads that have actually been reviewed still show `stale` and agents would pay for an extra request on every clean head (unconfirmed)

1.why: The diff takes pr-ready-state-core.mjs from 998 to 1077 lines. That is the known 'Split the growing ready-state core' defect at :750.

2.why: The change adds no new sibling module, so required_runtime_names at agent-autoreview.sh:4319-4325 already covers every imported file. The claim only matters if a hypothetical split happens.

3.why: pr-ready-state.md steps 5/8/10 do put the CodeRabbit request after the only projection pair. This is the known Major defect at pr-ready-state.md:408.

4.why: Run one after another, the marker does suppress repeat requests: a current-head marker gives 'requested'. The two-babysitter race is a speculative wording nitpick with no shown concurrent runner.

5.why: The issue-comment loop at core.mjs:771-783 has no author check. This restates the known 'Trust only authorized closeout requests' at :772.

6.why: classifyCodexReviewSignal is unchanged pre-existing code outside the diff. It never had a marker; any @codex review request counts on purpose, so this change adds no such gap.

7.why: isCodeRabbitFinalHeadReviewRequestBody does require the marker, and a test asserts plain requests don't count, so this is deliberate. A duplicate needs the human-triggered run to be missing after the check finishes, which the claim doesn't show.

8.why: The gates JSON example at pr-ready-state.md:276-298 still lists codexReviewSignal but not the new codeRabbitReviewSignal gate. The top-level field is missing from the example too, though the code emits both.

9.why: The claim labels itself unconfirmed and depends on unverified CodeRabbit behavior (edit-only follow-up runs). Nothing in the repo shows a clean run without a Run ID review.
